newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-HODGSON SAYS NO TO BLACKBURN, SET TO EXTEND AT INTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HODGSON SAYS NO TO BLACKBURN, SET TO EXTEND AT INTER.

text.p: English coach Roy Hodgson has turned down an offer to join former English premier league champions Blackburn Rovers and is set to extend his contract with Italian league leaders Internationale, club sources said on Wednesday.
They said the former Switzerland coach had informed the club, including chairman Massimo Moratti, that he had been approached but wanted to stay in Milan.
"You don't leave for a team way down the premier league when you're coaching the team at the top of serie A."
Blackburn, who won the English title in 1995, lie second from bottom in the premier league.

The source said the club was grateful to Hodgson for informing Inter of the approach and that he and Moratti were now certain to agree an extension of his contract, which he signed in October 1995. It is due to end in June, 1997.

Inter, who face a serie A derby against AC Milan next weekend, overwhelmed Boavista of Portugal 5-1 on Tuesday night in a UEFA Cup third round first leg tie that virtually ensured them a place in the quarter-finals next March.
Hodgson, whose job was the focus of media speculation earlier in the season, was quoted on Wednesday as saying he would stay with Inter "until 2005" if he had the chance.
Moratti said there was no way Hodgson would go to Blackburn.
"Hodgson came and told me about the offer he'd got," Corriere dello Sport quoted Moratti as saying.
"He asked me if I still had faith in him and I said yes."
